Kidney, lung and spleen (Kimmel , 2019)¶

The Kimmel dataset contains cells from lung, kindey and spleen. In this notebook, we will discard kidney and spleen cells and will focus on the lung dataset.

In this notebook:

  • Load the Kimmel dataset. We downloaded it from the GEO and each samples is provided as a separate GSM file, so we need to merge them and save it as an annData object.
  • We discard kidney and spleen cells and create an annData object that only contains lung cells.
  • We remove all cells coming from the Y1 mouse, because we observed that there was a big difference in coverage between those and the rest of the young cells, which lead to clustering solutions and UMAP projections were all the cells from Y1 clustered together rather than according to their cell type. We save a histogram with the distribution of counts.
  • Normalization and preprocessing.
  • Cell type annotation: we use the DEGs between angelidis cell types to annotate the Kimmel dataset in an unspuervised manner. We create a figure where the annotations are shown on the UMAP projection. We also create a dotplot showing the expression of the cell type markers used by Angelidis et al. on the Kimmel dataset.
  • Save annotated and preprocessed dataset: kimmel_annotated.h5ad.
  • Save table with cell type composition.
  • Create young and old annData objects.
  • Correct for confounding factors: downsample counts so that the number of counts/cell is comparable between the young and the old dataset.
  • Correct for confounding factors: downsample cells so that the number of cells per cell type is equal in the young and the old dataset.

INPUT:

  • Gene expression data obtained from GEO. Each GSM contains the data for a single sample. All gsm-s are stored in the directory .data/kimmel/gsm/.
  • DEGs between cell types from the Angelidis dataset.

OUTPUT:

  • Supplementary fig: histogram showing the distribution of counts of all the cells and where we can observe that cells from mouse Y1 have a markedly different distribution.
  • Supplementary fig: UMAP projection with predicted cell types.
  • Supplementary fig: dotplot showing cell-type marker expression on the predicted cell types.
  • Kimmel_annotated.h5ad: normalized and preprocessed gene expression data + metadata + cell type annotations.
  • Kimmel_cell_type_composition.csv: cell type composition in the Kimmel dataset.

Remove samples Y1L1 and Y1L2¶

Those two samples have too many counts compared to the rest of the samples, therefore, they cluster together and not according to the cell type. We tried preprocessing all the samples together and all of the cells drawn from mouse Y1 clustered together. We tried to correct for that batch effect by downsampling the counts so that all samples had the same amount of counts/cell. In addition, we used bbknn to correct for batch effects between samples. However, the batch effect was stronger and we observed that Y1 clustered together. We concluded that it was best to remove the two samples from mouse Y1. In addition to the batch effect, this also corrected for the imbalance between young and old samples: originally, there were 3 old samples and 4 young samples. This way we ended up with 3 young and 3 old samples.

Normalization & preprocessing¶

In [13]:
def normalization(adata):
    sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=200)
    sc.pp.filter_genes(adata, min_cells=3)
    sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, inplace=True)
    adata.var_names_make_unique()
    sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4)
    sc.pp.log1p(adata)
    return adata
In [14]:
def preprocessing(adata, batch_key):
    sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, min_mean=0.0125, max_mean=8, min_disp=0.1)
    sc.pp.pca(adata)
    if batch_key is None:
        print('Batch key is None, computing neighbors')
        sc.pp.neighbors(adata)
    else: 
        print(f'Using {batch_key} as batch_key to compute bbknn')
        sce.pp.bbknn(adata, batch_key=batch_key)
    sc.tl.umap(adata)
    return adata

Cell-type annotation¶

In their paper, Kimmel et al cell-type annotated their dataset by projecting the cell type labels from Tabula muris onto their dataset. Then, they manually curated their predicted labels. As their labels are not available and in order to make comparisons between the four lung datasets that we analyze in the present work, we predict the cell-type labels in the Kimmel dataset by using the DEGs obtained from the Angelidis dataset, which was expert-labeled.

Cell type composition in young and old¶

In [6]:
color_dic = dict(pd.read_csv('../../data/palettes/Cell_type_palette.csv', index_col=0)['color'])
In [7]:
df_ct = pd.DataFrame(index=sorted(list(set(adata.obs['cell_type'])), reverse=True), columns=['Young', 'Old'])
for ct in set(adata.obs['cell_type']):
    df_ct.loc[ct, 'Young'] = adata_young[adata_young.obs['cell_type'] == ct].shape[0]
    df_ct.loc[ct, 'Old'] = adata_old[adata_old.obs['cell_type'] == ct].shape[0]
    
    df_ct.loc[ct, 'Young_perc'] = 100*adata_young[adata_young.obs['cell_type'] == ct].shape[0]/adata_young.shape[0]
    df_ct.loc[ct, 'Old_perc'] = 100*adata_old[adata_old.obs['cell_type'] == ct].shape[0]/adata_old.shape[0]

Create input for enrichment analysis in R¶

In [10]:
df_comp = pd.DataFrame()
mice = set(adata.obs['mouse'])
cell_types = set(adata.obs['cell_type'])

for mouse in mice:
    for ct in cell_types:
        count = adata[(adata.obs['mouse']==mouse) & (adata.obs['cell_type']==ct)].shape[0] # same mouse, same cell-type
        total = adata[adata.obs['mouse']==mouse].shape[0] # same mouse, all cell types
        other = total - count # same mouse, cell types other than ct
        
        # Fill in dataframe
        group_id = f'{ct}_{mouse}'
        
        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Cell_type'] = ct
        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Mouse'] = mouse
        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Age'] = adata[adata.obs['mouse']==mouse].obs['age'][0] #it is impossible for the same mouse to have two different ages

        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Count'] = count
        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Other'] = other
        df_comp.loc[group_id, 'Total'] = total
df_comp.to_csv('../../output/tables/cell_type_enrichment/input/Kimmel_input_for_enrichment.csv')
